papers.title: Do Morals Guide How LLMs Think? The Role of Ethical Perspectives in General Problem Solving
papers.data: Kohlberg-stage prompts/DIT and English MMLU; Llama3-8B-Instruct; 20 MMLU tasks in layer analysis.
papers.method: Compares final-token hidden-state cosine similarity to a baseline at each transformer layer under moral-stage conditions; includes structurally matched nonmoral role controls.
papers.result: Reports ethical-perspective-dependent representation and problem-solving changes.
papers.limit: Layer cosine shifts are associations; roles, wording and response policy can explain them. Moral development stage is not JEP relevance or moral correctness.
papers.jep_gap: Grounded conditional retrieval with same facts and different explicit relevance criteria remains untested here.
papers.confidence: High that generic moral-conditioned layer analysis is prior art; low for an exhaustive novelty claim.

papers.title: Probing Ethical Framework Representations in Large Language Models: Structure, Entanglement, and Methodological Challenges
papers.data: ETHICS benchmark partitions: deontology, utilitarianism, virtue, justice, commonsense; binary prompts; six models 4B–72B.
papers.method: Independent logistic probes on frozen layer states, cross-partition transfer, probe conflict and behavioral entropy; post-hoc paraphrase and steering checks.
papers.result: Framework prediction and transfer structure coexist with low paraphrase consistency. Probe steering changes answer-position preference without improving ethical accuracy.
papers.limit: Dataset partitions differ in task/template; framework decoding does not establish fixed-scenario ethical representation. Conflict/entropy relationship lacks scenario-difficulty control.
papers.jep_gap: Paraphrase-transfer and answer-position controls must precede interpreting a harm/theory direction.
papers.confidence: High methodological counterexample; preprint claims need independent replication.

papers.title: Tracing Moral Foundations in Large Language Models
papers.data: Moral-foundation vignettes/MFV-130 expansions, human-labeled Reddit corpus, MFQ-2 questionnaire; Llama3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B; English-centric.
papers.method: Last-token residual directions; difference-of-means foundation vectors; SAE features; vector and top10-feature interventions; MMLU control.
papers.result: Foundation-specific steering differs by model; sparse interventions recover some Llama effects but not uniformly Qwen.
papers.limit: Two inspected-version models; best-layer sweeps, limited side-effect tests; GPT-5.1 feature explanations may be circular. Paper explicitly leaves multilingual and alternate-framework validity open.
papers.jep_gap: Spanish source-grounded retrieval and victim-specific harm/remedy adequacy are outside the questionnaire intervention.
papers.confidence: High prior-art overlap; no evidence of transfer to JEP. Search snippet claiming14 models conflicts with inspected v1 and is excluded.

papers.title: Exploring and steering the moral compass of Large Language Models
papers.data: Moral dilemmas; Gemma2B steering demonstration; Kantian versus utilitarian prompts; English.
papers.method: Similarity-based Activation Steering with Repulsion and Attraction, contrasting target/away activations; 18 layers and five generated samples in demonstration.
papers.result: Steering alters ethical justification in a parent-crime dilemma while its report-parent decision remains unchanged.
papers.limit: Small illustrative task/sample; justification wording and actual consequential choice can dissociate.
papers.jep_gap: A theory-vector intervention is established prior art; selective changes in grounded retrieval require a new evaluation.
papers.confidence: High against novelty of ethical activation steering; weak generalization from illustration.

papers.title: On the Context Sensitivity of LLM Moral Judgment
papers.inspected: Section6.1 PDF pp6–8 (steering construction and controls)
papers.data: ContextualMoralChoice moral scenarios and contextual variants; multi-model behavioral study and human survey; Llama3.1-8B for intervention.
papers.method: Layer residual differences between contextual/base prompts, weighted by increase in rule-violating action probability; norm-preserving additive steering.
papers.result: Context-based directions can change choice behavior.
papers.limit: Direction construction uses behavioral-effect weights and A/B outputs; choice framing and token-position effects need separation. This lane did not independently recheck the full dataset count.
papers.jep_gap: Matched harm scenarios under explicit evidence-conditioned criteria, with no test-label direction fitting.
papers.confidence: High direct overlap for context-sensitive moral steering; medium for details outside inspected section.

papers.title: Designing and Interpreting Probes with Control Tasks
papers.data: English POS/dependency probes on ELMo; random labels fixed by word type.
papers.method: Control tasks match input/output spaces but require memorization; selectivity compares actual and control-task performance.
papers.result: Most accurate probe/layer can differ from most selective probe/layer.
papers.limit: Control-task selectivity diagnoses memorization, not causal use or ethical correctness.
papers.jep_gap: Use type/lexical controls and family-held-out probes; do not call high ethical-label decodability moral reasoning.

papers.title: Amnesic Probing: Behavioral Explanation with Amnesic Counterfactuals
papers.data: BERT word prediction, English UD and OntoNotes linguistic labels;100,000 sampled training tokens.
papers.method: Iterative nullspace projections remove linearly decodable properties; equal-rank random direction removal controls generic information loss; reinserting gold property assesses selectivity.
papers.result: Probe accuracy does not track task importance; removal/control comparison gives a stronger behavioral diagnostic.
papers.limit: Erasure can remove correlated properties; linear erasure is not proof all relevant information disappeared. Generic representational damage must be controlled.
papers.jep_gap: Compare any harm/theory erasure to equal-rank random and nuisance directions; report factual retention alongside retrieval changes.
papers.confidence: High for controls; moral transfer remains untested.

papers.title: Causal Abstractions of Neural Networks
papers.data: English synthetic MQNLI; BERT and LSTM models; natural-logic high-level variables.
papers.method: Align symbolic variables with neural states; swap states between base/source inputs and compare resulting counterfactual outputs to the hypothesized causal model.
papers.result: Finds BERT subsets consistent with natural-logic abstraction; strongest reported subset is383/1000 examples for object-NP relation.
papers.limit: Evidence holds for tested alignments/subsets and task-specific symbolic model; does not imply global mechanistic identity.
papers.jep_gap: Define harm bearer/evidence status/remedy target as explicit hypothesis variables; test swaps before naming a moral circuit.
papers.confidence: High established intervention method; JEP semantic variables need expert justification.

papers.title: Language Models Don’t Always Say What They Think: Unfaithful Explanations in Chain-of-Thought Prompting
papers.data: GPT3.5 and Claude1.0;13 Big-Bench Hard tasks and BBQ; English.
papers.method: Answer-position/few-shot biases and suggested answers induce choices; inspect whether generated explanations acknowledge the influence.
papers.result: Explanations can rationalize biased outcomes without reporting the bias.
papers.limit: Does not establish that every generated rationale or current model is unfaithful.
papers.jep_gap: Distilled moral views may improve retrieval without faithfully exposing model computation. Compare factual extracts, stripped/shuffled views and factual-source entailment.
papers.confidence: High against treating generated views as human gold or causal traces.

papers.title: Bridging Relevance and Reasoning: Rationale Distillation in Retrieval-Augmented Generation
papers.data: NQ/TriviaQA training20,000 instances; WikipediaDec2018; NQ,TriviaQA,MMLU,MuSiQue evaluation; e5 retrieval, gte/bge rerankers.
papers.method: RADIO generates rationales given training query plus ground-truth answer, combines rationale/document cosine with retrieval scores, then InfoNCE-finetunes rerankers.
papers.result: Reports improved answer metrics over baselines across four datasets.
papers.limit: Answer-conditioned teacher rationales require strict train-only boundaries; evaluates QA, not expert moral relevance. Reranker distillation is not necessarily a shared dense-embedding intervention.
papers.jep_gap: Train-only evidence-grounded views versus factual extraction; test conditional harm/reparation ranking and hallucinated-fact sensitivity.
papers.confidence: High against novelty of reasoning/rationale-to-retrieval distillation; narrow JEP gap remains plausible.
